findings: BRIDGES 5/22 sentences (23%) connect to the one before. The approved iPhone 18 Pro script runs 53%; the weak generation of the same story ran 9%. A sentence that starts a new subject with no bridge reads as the next bullet, not the next beat. (framework S9, S22)

NO OPEN LOOP — nothing in the opening third points forward. Nothing promised early gets paid off later, so the ending summarises instead of arriving. The approved script plants one in sentence two ("only matters when you have no signal") and returns to it with "Back to that signal." (framework S2, S10, S18)

OPENING has no version, date or time anchor: 'WhatsApp is building a chat that WhatsApp itself says is not end'. A hook without context is confusion — the viewer should know WHICH thing and WHEN before the claim lands. (framework S1, S16)
NUMBERS: one every 4.6 sentences. The playbook asks for one every 2-3 — concrete numbers are what make a claim feel reported rather than asserted.
HUMANIZER: recorded for this draft. The checks above are the measurable half; the `humanizer` pass is the half that decides whether it sounds like a person.
